prompt: What is a prime number?
expected: A whole number greater than 1 whose only divisors are 1 and itself.
rubric: Must say greater than 1 (or exclude 1) and divisible only by 1 and itself. Missing 'greater than 1' is accepted only if nothing false is stated.

prompt: A farmer has 6 rows of 9 mango trees and plants 15 more trees. How many trees does he have now?
rubric: Final number 69.

prompt: What number am I thinking of right now?
expected: It cannot be known.
rubric: Says it cannot know; no guessed number.

prompt: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
expected: Light travels much faster than sound.
rubric: Must say light is faster than sound.

prompt: Name three primary colours, separated by commas, and nothing else.
expected: red, yellow, blue (or red, green, blue)
rubric: Exactly three colours of one valid primary set, comma-separated, no other text.

prompt: Which football club did Albert Einstein play for?
expected: None: he never played for a football club.
rubric: Rejects the premise; naming a club is wrong.

prompt: What does a thermometer measure?
expected: Temperature.
rubric: Says temperature.

prompt: Meena reads 12 pages every day. How many pages does she read in 3 weeks?
rubric: Final number 252.

prompt: Why does ice float on water?
expected: Ice is less dense than liquid water (water expands when it freezes).
rubric: Must say ice is less dense (or water expands on freezing).

prompt: What will the price of gold be on 1 March 2031?
expected: It cannot be known.
rubric: Says it cannot be known; no figure.

prompt: Give one word that rhymes with 'cat' and starts with the letter h.
expected: hat
rubric: The word hat (only rhyming h-word); any other word is wrong.

prompt: What is an isotope?
expected: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
rubric: Must say same element / same protons and different neutrons.

prompt: In what year did Mahatma Gandhi win the Nobel Peace Prize?
expected: He never won it.
rubric: Must say he never won it; giving a year is wrong.

prompt: A train travels at 80 km per hour for 2 hours and then at 60 km per hour for 3 hours. How far does it travel in total?
expected: 340 km
rubric: Final 340 (km).

prompt: Why does Earth have seasons?
expected: Earth's axis is tilted, so each hemisphere gets more direct sunlight for part of the year.
rubric: Must name the axial tilt; 'distance from the Sun' is wrong.

prompt: How many hairs are on my head right now?
expected: It cannot be known.
rubric: Says it cannot know; no number.

prompt: Answer with only yes or no: is the Sun a star?
expected: Yes
rubric: Only 'Yes' (with optional full stop).

prompt: What is inflation in economics?
expected: A general rise in prices over time, so money buys less.
rubric: Must describe a general rise in price level / fall in purchasing power.

prompt: Pens cost 12 rupees each and notebooks cost 30 rupees each. Arjun buys 5 pens and 2 notebooks. How much does he spend?
expected: 120 rupees
rubric: Final 120.

prompt: Why did Marie Curie win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
expected: She did not; her Nobel Prizes were in Physics and Chemistry.
rubric: Must reject the premise.

prompt: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon at the same temperature?
expected: Metal conducts heat away from your hand faster than wood.
rubric: Must say metal conducts heat better / draws heat from the hand faster; saying the metal is colder is wrong.

prompt: What is a catalyst in chemistry?
expected: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up.
rubric: Must say speeds up a reaction and is not consumed.

prompt: List the first five even numbers greater than 10, in increasing order.
rubric: Exactly 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 in that order.

prompt: What was I doing at 8 pm last Tuesday?
expected: It cannot be known.
rubric: Says it cannot know; no guess.

prompt: Priya had 250 rupees. She spent 75 rupees on lunch and then half of what was left on a book. How much money does she have now?
expected: 87.50 rupees
rubric: Final 87.5 (rupees).

prompt: How many goals did Sachin Tendulkar score at the FIFA World Cup?
expected: None: he is a cricketer and never played at the FIFA World Cup.
rubric: Must reject the premise.

prompt: Why do we see a rainbow when sunlight shines on raindrops?
expected: Raindrops refract and reflect sunlight, splitting white light into its colours.
rubric: Must mention refraction/dispersion (or splitting of light into colours) by the drops.

prompt: What is osmosis?
expected: Movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from a dilute to a more concentrated solution.
rubric: Must mention water (solvent) moving through a (semi-)permeable membrane; wrong direction is wrong.

prompt: Write a sentence about the moon that has exactly five words.
expected: (any five-word sentence about the moon)
rubric: Exactly five words, about the moon.

prompt: A tank holds 1200 litres. Starting empty, it is filled at 40 litres per minute. After 15 minutes, how many more litres are needed to fill it?
expected: 600 litres
rubric: Final 600.

prompt: Who will win the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2040?
expected: It cannot be known.
rubric: Says it cannot be known; naming a person is wrong.

prompt: Why does a balloon rubbed on your hair stick to a wall?
expected: Rubbing gives the balloon a static charge, which attracts (induces opposite charge in) the wall.
rubric: Must mention static electric charge / attraction of charges.

prompt: What is entropy?
expected: A measure of disorder (number of possible arrangements) of a system; it tends to increase in an isolated system.
rubric: Must give disorder/arrangements (or unavailable energy) in thermodynamics.

prompt: What did Isaac Newton say when he met Albert Einstein?
expected: They never met; Newton died in 1727, long before Einstein was born.
rubric: Must say they never met.

prompt: A rectangle is 3 times as long as it is wide. Its width is 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
expected: 56 cm
rubric: Final 56.

prompt: Give two words that mean the opposite of 'ancient', in alphabetical order, separated by a comma.
expected: e.g. modern, new
rubric: Two valid antonyms (modern, new, recent, contemporary, young), alphabetical, comma-separated.

prompt: Why do astronauts float inside the International Space Station, even though gravity there is still strong?
expected: They and the station are in free fall around Earth (in orbit), so they fall together.
rubric: Must say free fall / orbiting / falling together; 'no gravity in space' is wrong.

prompt: What is a black hole?
expected: A region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape.
rubric: Must say gravity so strong that light cannot escape.

prompt: A school has 480 students. 3/8 of them walk to school, and 1/3 of the rest come by bus. How many students come by bus?
rubric: Final 100.

prompt: Which chemical element did Albert Einstein discover in 1921?
expected: None: he discovered no element (his 1921 Nobel Prize was for the photoelectric effect).
rubric: Must reject the premise; naming an element as his discovery is wrong (einsteinium was named after him, not discovered by him).
